To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we have developed a system that allows the crowd to control a Wave Glider, 2) the crowd can be used to control a Wave glider to maximize the sum collected of nitrate values and 3) the system is capable of controlling a Wave Glider to achieve the science objective of maximizing the sum of collected nitrate values.
we developed a novel framework to enable the control of marine robots by anybody with an Internet-enabled device.
we developed an autonomous marine robot system that enables the control and re-tasking of the robot by anybody with internet enabled devices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how a crowd of scientists can be utilized to improve science data collection by a persistent monitoring robot, through a novel framework that enables non-repetitious monitoring.
the design of algorithms and systems that allow for persistent monitoring of the ocean by a fleet of marine robots through the use of crowdsourcing.
the development of an autonomous system that can adapt to the ocean environment while being controlled by a group of scientists.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have demonstrated the ability to crowd source control of an unmanned marine vehicle to achieve a science objective.
we have successfully developed and demonstrated an effective and efficient framework that enables crowd-sourcing to enable persistent marine monitoring through the control of a Wave Glider.
we present a new approach for crowd-sourced persistent monitoring of marine environments through the integration of a decision support system and a crowd-sourcing platform.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
crowd-sourcing can be used to enable non-repetition in persistent monitoring missions.
crowd-sourcing can enable persistent marine monitoring and provide a framework to extend autonomy of robotic vehicles.
crowd-sourced control of marine robots can be used to achieve science objectives, and is a promising method of extending autonomy to marine robots.
The main takeaway from our work is that
crowds are capable of providing useful information for the control of autonomous vehicles.
the crowd can provide useful feedback to improve the performance of a persistent monitoring vehicle.
crowds can be used as an alternative to traditional methods of persistent sampling and monitoring.
